speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the new movement symptoms you are experiencing and when they first started? I also need to know if you have recently started any new medications, particularly for psychiatric issues.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any involuntary muscle stiffness, tremors, or a slowing of your voluntary movements since starting the risperidone? I would also like to examine your neck and jaw for any signs of sustained muscle contractions or rhythmic movements.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: This sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Do you experience this restlessness internally as well, or is it purely motor-based, and have you noticed any worsening of symptoms when you try to sit still?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of recent risperidone initiation and subjective motor restlessness confirms the clinical picture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Antipsychotic-induced akathisia
